chunks.text: 43-year-old female, Associate Professional or Technician, resident of Tampines, Singapore.
Previous use of Alprazolam for anxiety (discontinued)
General Anesthesia with Propofol, Fentanyl, and Vecuronium; Maintenance with Sevoflurane and Remifentanil; Reversal with Neostigmine and Glycopyrrolate
Previous general anesthesia for laparoscopic appendectomy 10 years ago; no complications reported

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms./Mrs. [Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your surgery today. I'd like to go over a few things to make sure everything goes smoothly. Can you please tell me a bit about your medical history and why you're having this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, Doctor. I'm having my gallbladder removed because of the stones, right? I've had bad belly pain after eating, especially fatty food, and the scans showed stones in the gallbladder. So they decided on laparoscopic surgery.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for that. Let's go through your medical history. You have hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and obesity, correct?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, that's right. I've had diabetes for about 8 years now, and high blood pressure for even longer. My weight has been a problem for a while too.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: And your current medications are Metformin, Lisinopril, Atorvastatin, and Ranitidine, as per the records. Has there been any change in your medication list since your last hospital visit?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Actually, yes. The Ranitidine was stopped about six months ago because my acid problem got better. Now I'm taking Omeprazole 20mg once daily instead.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for letting me know. That's an important update. Do you have any known allergies, especially to medications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I had a rash when I took Penicillin before, so I'm allergic to that.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Got it. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia before? If so, how did you tolerate it?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first time. I've never had general anesthesia before, so I'm a bit nervous about it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's completely understandable. We'll make sure you're comfortable and safe throughout the process. Are you currently on any NPO orders? That is, when was your last meal or drink?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had my last meal around 8pm last night and a sip of water until about 10pm. I think I'm all set for fasting.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect, that sounds appropriate. Lastly, how would you describe your overall energy level and ability to perform daily activities?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I manage okay, but I do get tired more easily, especially after walking long distances. I can still do most of my daily tasks, though.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. It helps us understand your baseline. We'll be using general anesthesia with Propofol, Fentanyl, and Vecuronium to start, then maintain with Sevoflurane and Remifentanil. After surgery, we'll reverse the muscle relaxant with Neostigmine and Glycopyrrolate. Any questions so far?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all clear. I'm ready to proceed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. We'll take good care of you. You'll be seen by the surgical team shortly, and we'll be with you every step of the way.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] fentanyl twenty five micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:04] vecuronium ten milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] sevoflurane at two percent, remifentanil infusion started

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] blood pressure dropped to ninety over sixty, gave one hundred milliliters fluid bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:40] neostigmine two milligrams, glycopyrrolate four milligrams given for reversal

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:45] patient waking up, extubated smoothly

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm okay, I guess. A bit tired and my tummy is sore, but I'm awake at least.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. On a scale from 0 to 10, how would you rate your pain right now?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe a 4 or 5? It's manageable, but I can feel it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks. Are you feeling any nausea or like you might be sick?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A little bit, but not too bad. I didn't eat anything before, so maybe that helps.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. How's your breathing? Any difficulty or tightness in your chest?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I'm breathing fine. Just a bit stuffy from the tube, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Do you remember anything from the operation itself?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don't think so. I was out completely.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's expected. Lastly, with your diabetes and blood pressure, are you feeling any dizziness or unusual symptoms?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I feel stable. Just a bit thirsty, but I know I can't drink yet.

Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and hypertension
Obesity noted as a comorbidity
Currently taking Metformin 500mg Twice daily
Currently taking Lisinopril 10mg Once daily
Currently taking Atorvastatin 20mg Once daily
Previously took Ranitidine 150mg Once daily, but replaced with Omeprazole 20mg Once daily six months ago
Allergic to Penicillin (rash)
No known allergies to non-drug items (e.g., latex, adhesive bandages, foods) reported
No current respiratory symptoms or chronic respiratory conditions (e.g., asthma, COPD) reported
History of anxiety treated with Alprazolam, discontinued, with no current anxiety symptoms or treatments reported
First time undergoing general anesthesia
Last meal around 8pm the previous night, last drink (water) around 10pm, compliant with NPO orders
ASA-PS Class II (controlled hypertension and diabetes without systemic implications, mild obesity)
General Anesthesia planned with Propofol, Fentanyl, and Vecuronium for induction; maintenance with Sevoflurane and Remifentanil; reversal with Neostigmine and Glycopyrrolate
At 08:00, propofol 120 milligrams administered
At 08:02, fentanyl 25 micrograms administered
At 08:04, vecuronium 10 milligrams administered
At 08:05, endotracheal tube placed with grade one view
At 08:10, sevoflurane at 2% percent initiated
At 08:10, remifentanil infusion started
At 08:20, 100 milliliters fluid bolus administered due to blood pressure drop to 90 over 60
At 08:40, neostigmine 2 milligrams and glycopyrrolate 4 milligrams administered for reversal

Risk of Post-Operative Nausea and Vomiting (PONV) due to multiple contributing factors including obesity, female gender, and use of opioids (Fentanyl, Remifentanil) during anesthesia.
Airway watch due to obesity and potential for rapid desaturation, despite smooth extubation.
Glycemic control challenges post-operatively due to type 2 diabetes, potentially exacerbated by stress response to surgery and anesthesia.
Analgesia management considering the patient's opioid exposure (Fentanyl, Remifentanil) during surgery, which may lead to increased post-operative pain sensitivity or opioid requirements.
Hemodynamic instability watch, as indicated by intra-operative blood pressure drop requiring fluid bolus, which may persist or recur post-operatively.
Potential for delayed awakening or emergence delirium due to the use of Propofol and opioids, especially in a patient new to general anesthesia.

43-year-old female undergoing general anesthesia for the first time, with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and obesity. Patient is non-smoker, no current respiratory symptoms, and compliant with NPO orders.

Patient's current medications include Metformin, Lisinopril, and Atorvastatin. She has a history of anxiety treated with Alprazolam, which has been discontinued. Patient is allergic to Penicillin (rash).

Intra-operative course included administration of Propofol, Fentanyl, and Vecuronium for induction, with Sevoflurane and Remifentanil for maintenance. Reversal was achieved with Neostigmine and Glycopyrrolate. A fluid bolus was required for a blood pressure drop. Patient was extubated smoothly.

Monitor for post-operative nausea and vomiting (PONV), airway complications due to obesity, glycemic control challenges, potential for increased post-operative pain sensitivity, hemodynamic instability, and delayed awakening or emergence delirium.
Patient reports being 'okay' with soreness in the tummy and a pain level of 4 or 5 on a scale of 0 to 10.
Patient experiences mild nausea but notes it's 'not too bad' and possibly helped by not having eaten before surgery.
Patient reports no difficulty or tightness in the chest, only a 'bit stuffy' feeling attributed to the tube.
Patient recalls nothing from the operation itself, which is consistent with general anesthesia.
Patient feels stable with no dizziness or unusual symptoms related to diabetes or blood pressure.
Reversal agents (Neostigmine and Glycopyrrolate) were administered, and the patient woke up and was extubated smoothly.

open_questions.question: Can you confirm if there have been any changes to your medication list since it was recorded? Specifically, have you stopped, changed the dose, or replaced Metformin, Lisinopril, Atorvastatin, or Ranitidine?

Are you aware of any allergies or reactions to drugs (such as antibiotics, anesthetics, or painkillers), non-drug items (like latex, adhesive bandages, or foods), in addition to the documented Penicillin rash?
You have a history of resolved pneumonia 5 years ago. Do you currently have any respiratory symptoms, or have you been diagnosed with any chronic respiratory condition such as asthma or COPD?

You have a history of anxiety previously treated with Alprazolam, which has been discontinued. Are you currently experiencing any anxiety symptoms, or are you using any medications or therapies for anxiety?
Your prior general anesthesia for laparoscopic appendectomy 10 years ago was without complications. Have you had any other surgeries or procedures since then that involved anesthesia?
